papers.summary: SPaSM achieved 368.6 TFlop/s in double precision for a 48.96-billion-atom Lennard-Jones benchmark on 17 Roadrunner CUs (12,240 MPI ranks). Twenty-step timings use a hand count of 45 operations per pair interaction. The title rounds this to 369 Tflop/s; the PDF gives both 27.7% and approximately 28.3% of peak. A separate 36-million-atom copper EAM run demonstrates shock-ejecta physics.
papers.summary_kind: Editorial summary; not the original abstract

measurements.precision: Double (FP64); reciprocal starts from an FP32 estimate
measurements.scope: Aggregate benchmark time-step performance, not force-kernel-only
measurements.scale: 17 CUs / 12,240 MPI ranks, each host core paired with a Cell; 48.96 billion atoms; 20-step Fig. 4 timing; 45 counted operations per pair interaction divided by measured wall time.
measurements.measurement_method: Lightweight gettimeofday()-based event timers on Opteron processes, claimed overhead below 0.01%; only MPI rank 0 timers enabled for these measurements. Count N_pair interactions and divide 45 N_pair by cumulative wall time. Operation count includes force and potential energy; hand-coded Newton-Raphson reciprocal contributes nine operations with frest not counted, yielding 45 operations per LJ pair. Because SPU branching is expensive all pairs within the selected self/list subdomains are computed and out-of-cutoff contributions are zeroed.
